mots.sens: This word means 'Lord' or 'Master.' It is used to denote a higher authority, often in relation to God. In this verse, it emphasizes Jesus' position as the exalted Lord, seated at the right hand of God, which testifies to His sovereignty and divine authority, thereby reinforcing the understanding of His messianic role.

This term means 'to sit' or 'to remain.' In the context of this psalm, it evokes the idea of rest and a position of authority. The invitation to sit at the right hand of God symbolizes victory and the fulfillment of the mission, indicating that the Messiah has taken His place in heaven after triumphing over His enemies.

This word means 'enemy.' It designates those who oppose God and His kingdom. In this psalm, it is prophetic, announcing that the enemies of Christ will ultimately be subdued and that His victory will be complete, which brings great hope to believers regarding divine justice.

This term means 'footstool.' It symbolizes submission and dominion over enemies. In a spiritual sense, it indicates that Christ's reign is established and that all who oppose Him will ultimately be defeated, reinforcing the idea of God's ultimate victory over evil.

1.epoque: This psalm was written in an ancient context, probably during the reign of King David, a time when Israel sought to establish its national and spiritual identity in the face of surrounding enemies.
1.passage: Psalm 110 is a royal psalm that proclaims the majesty and reign of the Messiah. It is often cited in the New Testament to illustrate the divinity of Christ and His role as eternal sovereign.
1.culture: In Hebrew culture, sitting at the right hand of a king symbolizes supreme authority and special favor. This reflects the hierarchy and importance of power relations in the Old Testament.
1.interpretation: This verse announces Christ's victory over His enemies and His exalted position at the right hand of God. It highlights the messianic character of Jesus, who is both king and priest, interceding for us before the Father.
1.commentaire: This psalm reminds us that, although we may face adversities, the victory belongs to Christ. As believers, we are called to live in trust and hope, knowing that our Lord reigns with power and that His enemies will ultimately be defeated. This encourages us to persevere in our faith and to proclaim His reign in our lives.

mots.sens: This word means 'scepter' or 'staff,' symbolizing authority and power. It is often associated with royalty and governance. In the context of this verse, it emphasizes the divine sovereignty that extends from Zion, indicating that God's reign is established on earth through His Messiah. Spiritually, this reminds believers that Christ, as King, has authority over all things, including our lives.

This term means 'until' or 'in,' indicating a scope or continuity. In this verse, it emphasizes that the Messiah's dominion extends even in the midst of His enemies. This evokes the idea that, despite opposition, God's power is manifest and active, bringing assurance to believers that God is sovereign in all circumstances.

This word means 'enemy' and designates those who oppose God's will. In the context of this verse, it reminds us that the presence of the enemy does not diminish God's power. Theologically, this teaches us that even in the face of opposition, Christ's victory is certain, calling us to faith and trust in His power.

2.epoque: This psalm was written in a context where Israel was seeking restoration and sovereignty, probably under the influence of the Davidic monarchy.
2.passage: Psalm 110 is a messianic royal psalm that announces the victory of the Messiah and His eternal reign. It is often cited in the New Testament to illustrate the divinity and authority of Jesus Christ.
2.culture: In Hebrew culture, the scepter was a symbol of power and legitimacy. The fact that God extends this scepter from Zion underscores the importance of the holy city as the center of divine presence and royalty.
2.interpretation: This verse announces the Messiah's dominion over His enemies, affirming that even in times of conflict, divine power is at work. It reminds believers that, despite struggles, victory belongs to God and His Christ.
2.commentaire: This passage encourages us to recognize God's sovereignty in our lives, even when we face challenges. As Christians, we are called to live under the reign of Christ, to trust Him, and to move forward with confidence, knowing that His power is at work amid our adversities.

mots.sens: This word means 'people' and often designates the community or nation as a whole. In this verse, it evokes the people of God, who gather with fervor and enthusiasm to serve the Lord. The theological scope here emphasizes the importance of unity and the commitment of the people in the divine mission.

This term means 'grace' or 'favor,' and it is often used to describe an inner beauty or spiritual quality. In the context of this verse, it evokes the 'sacred ornaments' that symbolize the beauty and purity of worship rendered to God. This reminds us that worship must be done with a pure heart and sincere intention.

This word means 'dew' and refers to the freshness and vitality that dew brings to the earth. Spiritually, this symbolizes renewal and divine blessing. In this verse, the youth that comes like dew evokes the promise of life and renewal that God grants to those who follow Him.

3.epoque: Psalm 110 is attributed to David and reflects a period when Israel was seeking stability and spiritual direction under the monarchy.
3.passage: This psalm is a royal song that announces the messianic reign of Christ. It emphasizes God's sovereignty and the importance of the people's faithfulness in worship and service.
3.culture: In Hebrew culture, the gathering of the people for worship was an essential communal act, symbolizing unity and devotion to God. The sacred ornaments were often associated with rituals of consecration and praise.
3.interpretation: This verse highlights the fervor and commitment of God's people when they gather to worship. The youth that comes like dew symbolizes the spiritual renewal that God brings to His people, strengthening their faith and devotion.
3.commentaire: This psalm reminds us of the importance of gathering as a community of believers to worship God with passion. It encourages us to seek spiritual renewal and to be clothed in the beauty of divine grace in our service. As Christians, we are called to be that youth who rises with zeal for the Kingdom of God, bringing the freshness of dew into our lives and the lives of others.

mots.sens: This name means 'king of righteousness' and evokes a mysterious and significant figure in biblical history. Melchizedek is both king of Salem and priest of the Most High God, symbolizing an eternal priesthood that transcends the Mosaic law. In this verse, he represents the perfect model of the priesthood of Jesus Christ, who is both king and priest, thus establishing a new covenant.

This verb means 'to turn around' or 'to surround', and in this context, it emphasizes the permanence and immutability of God's oath. The idea that God will not repent of His commitment reinforces the certainty of the promise made to Jesus as an eternal priest. This underscores the importance of divine faithfulness and the security we have in Christ.

The term means 'priest' and refers to one who is called to serve in worship and act as an intermediary between God and humanity. In the context of this verse, it highlights the unique role of Jesus as the eternal priest, who offers a perfect sacrifice for sin, thus establishing a direct relationship between God and humanity.

4.epoque: This psalm was written at a time when Israel was under monarchy, probably during the reign of David, reflecting the political and spiritual concerns of that period.
4.passage: Psalm 110 is a royal psalm that proclaims the sovereignty of God and the majesty of the king. It establishes a link between the royalty of David and the priesthood of Melchizedek, thus announcing the coming of a Messiah who will unite these two functions.
4.culture: In Hebrew culture, the role of priest was crucial for mediation between God and the people. Melchizedek, as a unique figure, illustrates a priesthood that is not limited by the Mosaic law, thus foreshadowing the priesthood of Christ.
4.interpretation: This verse emphasizes the eternal nature of Jesus' priesthood, which is based on a divine oath. It demonstrates that His ministry is superior to that of the Levitical priests, establishing a new covenant that is permanent and unshakeable.
4.commentaire: This passage reminds us that Jesus is our eternal priest, interceding for us before God. By understanding the depth of His ministry, we are encouraged to approach Him with confidence, knowing that He is faithful to His promises. It also calls us to live in accordance with this reality, recognizing His authority and committing ourselves to serve in His kingdom.

mots.sens: This term designates a master or lord. It evokes authority and sovereignty, and in this context, it emphasizes Christ's position as the supreme Lord, seated at the right hand of God. This notion of lordship is essential for understanding Christ's reign over all things and His ability to exercise divine judgment.

This word means 'to break' or 'to crush'. It is often associated with the idea of defeating enemies or judging with power. In this verse, it highlights God's divine action against kings and the mighty who oppose Him, thus affirming God's sovereignty in human affairs.

This term means 'kings'. It represents those who hold power and authority on earth. In the context of this verse, it alludes to those who stand against God, illustrating the struggle between good and evil, and the certainty that God, through His Son, will triumph over all earthly authority.

This word means 'day'. It is often used in Scripture to designate a specific time, often related to a divine action or judgment. In this verse, it evokes the 'day of His anger', a moment when God will exercise His judgment, reminding us of the importance of living in the fear of God and recognizing His authority.

5.epoque: This psalm was written at a time when Israel faced powerful enemies, and it reflects the people's aspirations for a just and victorious king.
5.passage: Psalm 110 is a royal and messianic psalm, often interpreted as a prophecy concerning the reign of Christ. It establishes Christ's position as sovereign and judge, affirming His authority over the nations.
5.culture: In Hebrew culture, royalty was associated with divine authority. Kings were seen as representatives of God on earth, and their judgment was perceived as an extension of divine justice.
5.interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's power through Christ, who, as Lord, exercises judgment over the kings and the mighty of this world. It reminds believers that, even in the face of opposition, God reigns with authority and justice.
5.commentaire: This psalm encourages us to put our trust in God, knowing that He is sovereign and that He breaks the plans of the mighty who oppose Him. As Christians, we are called to live in the light of this truth, to proclaim the lordship of Christ, and to prepare for His return, when He will exercise just judgment over all humanity.

mots.sens: This verb means 'to judge' or 'to exercise justice'. It evokes the idea of divine judgment, where God establishes truth and justice among the nations. In this context, it underscores God's sovereignty over the peoples and His role as the supreme judge, bringing retribution to those who have sinned. It also reminds us of the theological scope of divine justice, which is both an act of judgment and a promise of restoration for those who turn to Him.

This term designates a 'nation' or 'people'. In the Bible, it can refer to pagan nations or ethnic groups. Here, it highlights the universal scope of God's judgment, which is not limited to Israel but extends to all nations. It reminds us that God is the Lord of all peoples and that He has authority over all of creation.

This word means 'head' or 'chief'. It can symbolize authority or power. In this verse, 'to break heads' evokes the destruction of leaders or the mighty who oppose divine will. It indicates that God does not hesitate to bring down those who abuse their power and lead nations into injustice.

6.epoque: This psalm is attributed to David and is set in a context where Israel faces external threats, notably from enemy nations. It reflects the era of the kings of Israel, where military power and divine sovereignty were major concerns.
6.passage: Psalm 110 is a messianic psalm that announces the kingship and priesthood of Christ. It establishes God's victory over His enemies and the promise of an eternal reign, highlighting the duality of Christ's role as both king and priest.
6.culture: In Hebrew culture, judgment and justice were central themes, often associated with God's faithfulness to His people. Images of war and conquest were common, symbolizing the struggle between good and evil, and God's victory over His adversaries.
6.interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's power as the judge of the nations and the fulfillment of His redemptive plan. It reminds us that divine justice is exercised not only over Israel but over all nations, and that God has the power to overturn the unjust and restore order.
6.commentaire: This passage reminds us that God is sovereign over all nations and that He will exercise His justice in His time. As believers, we must find comfort in the certainty that God is the ultimate judge and that, even in difficult times, His justice will prevail. It also calls us to live in justice and to be instruments of peace in a world often troubled.

mots.sens: This word means 'to lift' or 'to carry.' In the context of this verse, it evokes the idea of rising up or being exalted after going through trials. It emphasizes the victory and strength that come after a time of struggle, which is particularly relevant for the Messiah, who, after His suffering, is exalted at the right hand of God.

This term refers to a 'torrent' or 'stream,' symbolizing a source of life and refreshment. In this verse, it represents the spiritual resources that the Messiah receives to accomplish His mission. It highlights the idea that, even in times of difficult walking, there is a divine provision that enables one to rise up.

This word refers to 'drinking' or 'to be nourished,' indicating an act of receiving and feeding. In the context of this verse, it symbolizes the necessity of drawing from spiritual resources to be strengthened. It underscores the importance of dependence on God to obtain the strength needed to move forward.

7.epoque: This psalm was written in a context where Israel was seeking spiritual and political direction, often confronted with enemies and internal challenges.
7.passage: Psalm 110 is a royal and messianic psalm, where King David speaks of the sovereignty and priesthood of the Messiah, announcing His victory over His enemies and His exaltation beside God.
7.culture: In Hebrew culture, drinking from the torrent symbolizes dependence on God for strength and spiritual refreshment. It also evokes the idea that spiritual leaders must draw from divine resources to guide their people.
7.interpretation: This verse illustrates how the Messiah, in going through trials, finds His strength in communion with God. It shows that even in times of difficulty, it is possible to rise up and be exalted by divine grace.
7.commentaire: This passage reminds us of the importance of seeking our strength in God, especially when facing challenges. Like the Messiah, we are called to draw from the sources of life that God offers us, in order to rise up and walk with assurance. In times of trial, let us take the time to nourish ourselves spiritually to be renewed and restored.
